examples: There are too many subjects this term.
nuance: 과목 is a school subject like math or science that you study in class. To say a subject you like Koreans use 좋아하는 과목 with the verb in front.
mistakes: Confusing 과목 the subject with 수업 the class period

examples: Math is really hard for me.
My friend is very good at math.
nuance: 수학 is the school subject of mathematics with numbers and equations. Koreans say 수학을 잘하다 to mean being good at it, using the verb 잘하다.
mistakes: Saying 수학을 어렵다 instead of 수학이 어렵다

examples: Science is the most fun for me.
We did an experiment in science today.
nuance: 과학 is the school subject of science covering things like nature and experiments. The teacher who teaches it is a 과학 선생님, placing 과학 in front as a modifier.
mistakes: Confusing 과학 the science with 과목 the subject

nuance: 역사 means history, both the school subject and the story of the past. Korean history is 한국 역사, with the country name placed in front as a modifier.
mistakes: Using 옛날 for the school subject instead of 역사

examples: I like the art class period.
We draw pictures in art class.
The art teacher is very kind.
nuance: 미술 is the school subject of art where students draw and paint. The class period for it is 미술 시간, and you draw a picture with the verb 그림을 그리다.
mistakes: Confusing 미술 the art subject with 그림 a picture

examples: We played soccer in PE today.
내일은 체육 시간이 두 번 있어요.
Tomorrow there are two PE periods.
nuance: 체육 is physical education, the school subject where students exercise and play sports. The special clothes you wear for it are 체육복, with 체육 placed in front.
mistakes: Using 운동 the exercise for the school subject 체육

examples: We saw a world map in geography.
nuance: 지리 is geography, the subject about places, maps, and the land. In class you often look at a map, which is 지도, a similar but different word.
mistakes: Confusing 지리 the geography with 지도 the map

examples: My grades are good this term.
The grades come out next week.
I want to receive good grades.
nuance: 성적 means the grades or scores you get for school work. Koreans say 성적이 나오다 when results are released and 성적을 받다 when you get them.
mistakes: Confusing 성적 the grades with 시험 the exam itself

examples: What grade is your sibling in now.
I became second grade this year.
We are in the same grade.
nuance: 학년 means a school grade or year level, such as first or second grade. To ask which one Koreans say 몇 학년 using the question word 몇 for numbers.
mistakes: Confusing 학년 the grade level with 학교 the school

examples: What is your major at university.
I have not decided a major yet.
nuance: 전공 is your major, the main field you study at university. Koreans say 전공을 정하다 to decide one and 전공을 바꾸다 to change it later.
mistakes: Using 과목 a school subject when you mean a university 전공

examples: I attend an English academy in the evening.
nuance: 학원 is a private academy where students take extra lessons after regular school. To attend one regularly Koreans use the verb 다니다, as in 학원에 다니다.
mistakes: Confusing 학원 the academy with 학교 the regular school

examples: I came to Korea to study abroad.
My sister went abroad to study in America.
I want to study abroad in Japan.
nuance: 유학 means going to a foreign country to study, often for a degree. Koreans say 유학을 가다 to leave for it and 유학을 오다 when someone comes to their country.
mistakes: Using 여행 a trip when you mean long term 유학
